newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran sends first oil to new Bandar Abbas refinery.
newsitem.headline: Iran sends first oil to new Bandar Abbas refinery.

text.p: Iran has delivered the first 60,000 tonne cargo of heavy crude oil to its new 232,000 barrels per day (bpd) refinery project at Bandar Abbas, the English-language Tehran Times newspaper reported on Tuesday.
"This is the first delivery of heavy crude oil which is being stored in the refinery's storage tanks," the paper said.
The $1.6 billion Bandar Abbas refinery, which would be Iran's eighth major plant, will be inaugurated in May and would serve both domestic and export markets, Tehran Times reported.
"The main goal of setting up the Bandar Abbas refinery is to meet a part of the country's requirements and exporting the surplus," the paper said.

Iranian energy officials have said that a crude unit would be the first to be commissioned and that runs would gradually be increased at Bandar Abbas, eventually allowing the OPEC state to become self-sufficient in oil products.

Bandar Abbas is expected to eventually produce 46,100 bpd of gasoline, 36,200 bpd of kerosene and jet fuel, 69,500 bpd of gas oil, 66,500 bpd of heavy fuel oil, 7,100 bpd of liquefied petroleum gas, 5,000 bpd of tar and 124 tonnes of sulphur a day.
Iran's current refining capacity stands at 1.24 million bpd.
